# Practice Job Interview Questions with DeepSeek

> **In short:** DeepSeek is a free AI assistant you can use in any browser. Open it, ask it to play the role of an interviewer, and it will ask you common questions, score your answers, and suggest stronger wording. It cannot read your face or hear your voice, so pair it with a real video call for full practice.

Job interviews make almost everyone nervous. The good news: a few hours of practice in front of an honest audience can turn that nervous energy into confidence. DeepSeek (a free AI chat assistant) makes a surprisingly patient practice partner — it can take the role of a hiring manager, throw realistic questions at you, give you feedback, and even rewrite your answers in a sharper way. This guide walks you through exactly how to set that up, step by step, even if you have never opened an AI chat tool before.

## Before you start
- **A free DeepSeek account.** Sign up at deepseek.com with an email address or a Google account. The free tier is enough for this guide.
- **A device with a browser.** A laptop is easiest because the screen is bigger, but a phone or tablet works too.
- **About 30–45 minutes.** The first run-through takes longer; once you know the pattern, a 10-minute warm-up is plenty.
- **The job description (optional but helpful).** If you have a real posting in mind, keep it open in another tab so you can paste key details into the chat.

## Step 1 — Open DeepSeek and start a new chat
Go to **deepseek.com** in your browser and sign in. After login you'll land on the main chat screen — a wide, mostly empty page with a text box at the bottom. Look for a small **"New Chat"** button or a **pencil/plus icon** near the top of the conversation list. Click it. The text box clears and you're ready to type. If you don't see a "New Chat" button, refresh the page; DeepSeek usually opens a fresh conversation by default. **You'll know it worked when** the text box is empty, no previous messages are visible, and a blinking cursor sits in the input area.

## Step 2 — Set the role and the job
Type a short setup message that tells DeepSeek who it should pretend to be and what job you are practicing for. The more concrete you are, the more useful the questions will be. Think of it like handing a real interview coach a one-page brief. Paste this into the box, then edit the bracketed parts to match your situation.
💬 Example: *"Act as a friendly hiring manager interviewing me for a [Customer Support Specialist] role at a mid-size company. Ask me one question at a time, wait for my answer, then give brief feedback and the next question. Keep questions realistic for this job."*
Hit **Enter** (or tap the **paper-plane / send arrow**). A few seconds later, DeepSeek will reply confirming the role and asking the first interview question. **You'll know it worked when** the first question appears within 10–15 seconds and clearly relates to the job you named.

## Step 3 — Answer the question like it's real
Read the question, take a breath, and type your answer as you would actually say it out loud. Don't try to be perfect — the whole point of practice is to hear how you sound before you say it for real. If the question is "Tell me about a time you dealt with a difficult customer," answer with a real story, not a textbook definition. Aim for two to four sentences. The **Shift + Enter** key combination usually adds a new line, while **Enter** alone sends the message. **You'll know it worked when** DeepSeek's reply shows specific feedback (what was strong, what was missing) and then asks the next question. If the reply is just "Great, next question," prompt it: *"Can you tell me what was strong in my answer and what I should add?"*

## Step 4 — Ask for a stronger version of your answer
Once you have answered two or three questions this way, you have raw material to work with. Pick the answer that felt weakest, or the one for the most important question, and ask DeepSeek to rewrite it. Be specific about the tone you want.
💬 Example: *"Here's my answer to your last question: '[paste your answer]'. Please rewrite it to sound more confident, around 90 words, with a clear result at the end."*
Read the rewrite out loud — that's the part most people skip, and it's where the practice actually sticks. **You'll know it worked when** the rewritten version is shorter, punchier, and you can say it naturally in under a minute.

## Step 5 — Ask for the questions you fear most
Every job has a few questions that make candidates freeze: *"What's your biggest weakness?"*, *"Why are you leaving your current job?"*, *"Where do you see yourself in five years?"*. Ask DeepSeek for the full list, plus a model answer for each. This gives you a safety net so nothing in the real interview catches you off guard.
💬 Example: *"Give me the 8 most common interview questions for a [Customer Support Specialist] role, and a short model answer for each in plain language."*
The model answers won't be your words — and that's the point. Use them as a starting template, then rewrite them in Step 6 so they sound like you. **You'll know it worked when** you have a written list of questions and sample answers you can scroll through on your phone right before the real interview.

## Step 6 — Run a final mock interview, one question at a time
Now switch into test mode. Tell DeepSeek to behave like a real interviewer with no feedback between questions, just like in the actual room. Type your answers as if you had two minutes to think, then send. At the end, ask for an overall score and three things to improve. This single run-through usually surfaces the gaps your earlier practice hid.
💬 Example: *"Let's do a 5-question mock interview now. No feedback between questions, just like a real interview. After the last answer, give me an overall score out of 10 and three specific things to improve."*
**You'll know it worked when** you finish the five questions without checking your notes, and the final score gives you a clear list of what to work on next.

## Common mistakes
- **Skipping the role setup.** If you just type "ask me interview questions," you'll get generic lists instead of a back-and-forth conversation. Always set the role in Step 2.
- **Treating the AI's feedback as the final word.** DeepSeek's suggestions are a starting point, not gospel. If a rewrite doesn't sound like you, say so and ask for another version — it's free to keep asking.
- **Practicing only by reading.** Reading sample answers in your head is not the same as typing them out loud. Always speak the final version at least once, because the real interview uses your voice, not your eyes.
- **Forgetting what the tool can't do.** DeepSeek can't see your face, hear your tone, or notice that you're fidgeting. For a real dress rehearsal, pair this guide with a video recording of yourself, or ask a friend to mock-interview you on a video call.

## What this means for you
- **In everyday life:** You walk into your next interview with a short list of practiced stories and a few strong sentences already in your mouth. The nerves don't disappear, but the "blank mind" feeling does.
- **For your business or work:** If you manage or hire people, this same trick works in reverse. Use DeepSeek to generate realistic interview questions for the roles you need to fill, so every candidate gets a fairer, more consistent first round.
- **If you're just getting started:** One 20-minute session before bed for three nights in a row is more useful than one five-hour cram session. Consistency beats intensity.

## Try it now
Open deepseek.com, paste this exact message, and answer the first question it gives you: *"Act as a friendly hiring manager. Ask me one common interview question at a time. After I answer, give me two lines of feedback and the next question. Start now."* Set a 10-minute timer and see how far you get.
